To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Longer (GT)n repeats, which regulate HMOX1 transcriptional activity, are associated with higher HMOX1 plasma levels and reduced risk of ARDS.
longer HMOX1 microsatellite repeats are associated with higher HO-1 plasma levels and reduced ARD risk.
the common S allele of the HO-1 promoter microsatellite (GT)n is associated with increased risk of ARDS, and that the common haplotype containing the S allele is also associated with ARDS.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the association of HMOX-1 polymorphism with the development of ARDS.
the association between HMOX1 gene polymorphisms and acute respiratory distress syndrome risk.
the role of HMOX-1 in ARDS.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the (GT)n microsatellite polymorphisms and haplotypes in the HMO1 gene promoter are associated with ARDS development.
the HMOX-1 (GT)n microsatellite polymorphisms are associated with the ARDS development and plasma HO- 1 levels.
the HMOX gene variation is associated with ARDS.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the longer (GT)n repeat allele is associated with higher plasma heme-oxygenase-1 levels and decreased risk of acute respiratory distress.
the longer (GT)n repeat is associated with higher plasma HMO-1 level and reduced ARDS development.
the HMOX-1 gene polymorphisms and haplotypes were associated with the risk of ARDS and plasma HO- 1 levels.
The main takeaway from our work is that
HMOX polymorphisms may be associated with ARDS susceptibility.
HMOX-1 variation may modulates ARDS risk through a promoter microsatellite.
the HO-1 promoter microsatellite is a novel ARDS susceptibility locus that modulates the risk of developing ARDS.
